PETRA ZLATARIĆ-NOVOSEL
Machine Learning Engineer | NLP & Document AI
Osijek, Croatia | petra.zlataric@example.com | +385 55 555 0606 | github.com/pzn-ml-example

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Machine Learning Engineer with 5+ years of experience across NLP, data science and research, including deploying machine learning systems to production. Specialised in document classification and named entity recognition for Croatian administrative text. Experienced in taking models from dataset preparation and experimentation through model serving and production monitoring, using Python, MLflow and Azure. Currently pursuing a PhD in computer science focused on Croatian-language NLP.

PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE

Machine Learning Engineer | Slavonica Document AI d.o.o. | Osijek
03/2023–Present
- Developed and deployed a classifier for scanned incoming public-administration documents, achieving 94% accuracy and 0.91 macro F1 across 23 classes; the service processes approximately 15,000 documents per day.
- Fine-tuned XLM-R and BERTić transformer models for document classification and named entity recognition in Croatian administrative text, including persons, organisations, OIB numbers, addresses and legal references.
- Built an annotated dataset of 4,000 documents, developed annotation guidelines and coordinated two annotators; achieved an inter-annotator kappa of 0.87.
- Served models as FastAPI services in Docker on Azure App Service; used Azure ML and MLflow for experimentation and model registry.
- Established weekly production monitoring for text length, vocabulary and predicted-class distribution, with alerts for PSI above 0.2. Detected a client-side OCR change associated with a 9-point accuracy drop and helped resolve it within a week.
- Mentor two student interns.

Data Scientist | Baranjska kreditna banka d.d. | Zagreb (remote from Osijek)
09/2021–02/2023
- Developed customer churn prediction models using gradient boosting and LightGBM for the sales team.
- Built a customer complaint topic-classification workflow, progressing from TF-IDF and logistic regression to fastText; classified 11 topics for weekly reporting to customer service management.
- Prepared SQL reports from an Oracle data warehouse.

Research Project Assistant | Faculty of Applied Informatics, University of Drava
10/2020–08/2021
- Created a corpus of Croatian legal texts and annotated data; wrote supporting Python scripts.

SELECTED PROJECT

Retrieval-Augmented Question Answering Demo | Personal project | 2025
- Built a weekend prototype for question answering over Croatian laws using a sentence-embedding model, FAISS and an open-weight LLM accessed through an API.
- Prototype only; not used in production and checked manually without formal evaluation.

EDUCATION
PhD studies in Computer Science | University of Drava | 2022–Present
Research topic: Named entity recognition in Croatian legal texts | Expected completion: 2027

MSc in Computer Science (Mag. ing. comp.) | University of Drava | 2020

CERTIFICATIONS & TEACHING
Microsoft Certified: Azure AI Engineer Associate | 2024
Guest Lecturer, NLP Summer School | 2025 (90-minute lecture)

TECHNICAL SKILLS
Programming and data: Python, SQL, pandas, NumPy
Machine learning and NLP: PyTorch, Hugging Face Transformers, scikit-learn, LightGBM, fastText, spaCy, sentence-transformers, TF-IDF
Production ML and MLOps: MLflow, FastAPI, Docker, Azure ML, Azure App Service, Azure Functions, Evidently, model serving, production monitoring
Data and tools: Oracle SQL, PostgreSQL, FAISS, Label Studio, Git, Linux

LANGUAGES
Croatian: Native | English: C1 (regular English-language client meetings) | German: B2

PUBLICATION
Zlatarić-Novosel, P. et al. (2024). “Named Entity Recognition for Croatian Administrative Documents.” Regional workshop on Slavic language processing.

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, well-structured CV with clear progression from research and data science into production machine learning engineering. It uses quantified outcomes effectively, including 94% accuracy, 0.91 macro F1, 15,000 documents per day, 4,000 annotated documents, kappa 0.87, and a 9-point production accuracy drop. The current role demonstrates genuine ownership across dataset creation, model development, serving, monitoring, and mentoring. The RAG project is presented honestly as a prototype rather than being overstated as production experience. The main limitation is that some job-relevant engineering capabilities are not demonstrated, particularly feature engineering, data ingestion pipelines, CI/CD, automated testing, and explicit data versioning; these are candidate-experience gaps rather than writing defects.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: ATS compatibility is very good. The CV uses conventional headings, readable date formats, standard bullet points, searchable technology names, and no apparent tables, graphics, columns, or unusual formatting that would impair parsing. It contains strong matches for Python, Azure, Azure ML, MLflow, FastAPI, Docker, model serving, production monitoring, Hugging Face Transformers, NLP, document classification, NER, and RAG. Estimated AI/ATS screening probability is high, approximately 85–90% for this vacancy, although the score may be reduced by the absence of the exact concepts “feature engineering,” “data ingestion pipelines,” and “data versioning.” The CV also shows only MLflow among the listed MLOps/orchestration examples, which is sufficient for the stated familiarity requirement but narrower than the full job description.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The CV aligns very well with the core role: it shows a relevant computer science degree, production ML deployment, strong Python and NLP experience, Azure, MLflow, model serving, monitoring, text-data preparation, and a truthful RAG prototype. The customer-support relevance is supported by the complaint topic-classification workflow used for customer service reporting, although the main production experience is in document AI rather than support assistants. The candidate's material shows a gap against the requirement for at least four years specifically as a machine learning engineer shipping systems to production: the documented ML Engineer role begins in 03/2023, while earlier experience is as a data scientist and research assistant. The candidate's material also does not establish feature engineering or data ingestion pipelines, and it does not explicitly establish data versioning beyond the MLflow model registry. These are requirement gaps, not CV-writing defects. Team contribution is credibly supported by mentoring two interns, coordinating annotators, guest lecturing, and regular English-language client meetings. No unsupported culture or work-arrangement claims are made.
critique.improvement_instructions:
MINOR ATS/TARGETING ENHANCEMENTS:
1. In the Technical Skills section under “Production ML and MLOps,” make the existing supported capabilities more keyword-explicit by changing the line to: “MLflow, model registry, FastAPI model serving, Docker, Azure ML, Azure App Service, Azure Functions, Evidently, production monitoring, data-drift monitoring.” Do not add data versioning, orchestration platforms, CI/CD, or automated testing unless the candidate can substantiate them.
2. In the current Slavonica Document AI role, revise the Azure/MLflow bullet from “Served models as FastAPI services in Docker on Azure App Service; used Azure ML and MLflow for experimentation and model registry” to “Implemented model serving with FastAPI and Docker on Azure App Service; used Azure ML and MLflow for experimentation and model registry.” This preserves the existing facts while matching the job’s “model serving” terminology more directly.
3. In the Data Scientist role, make the customer-support relevance more searchable by revising “Built a customer complaint topic-classification workflow, progressing from TF-IDF and logistic regression to fastText; classified 11 topics for weekly reporting to customer service management” to “Built a customer complaint topic-classification workflow for customer-service reporting, progressing from TF-IDF and logistic regression to fastText; classified 11 topics across 11 categories.” Use the latter wording only if “11 topics across 11 categories” accurately reflects the work; otherwise retain the current wording and add only “for customer-service reporting.”
critique.critical_issues:
Claims the sources (the candidate's own material; for the employer, the job ad and company research) do not support:
- “coordinated two annotators”

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, well-structured CV with clear chronology, professional presentation, relevant technical skills, and excellent use of measurable outcomes. The strongest evidence includes 94% accuracy, 0.91 macro F1, 23 document classes, approximately 15,000 documents per day, a 4,000-document annotated dataset, kappa of 0.87, and a documented nine-point production accuracy drop. The CV also handles the PhD status and RAG project honestly, without overstating either. The main content limitation is not a writing defect: several requirements in the advertisement are not supported by the candidate information, particularly four full years specifically as a production ML Engineer, data versioning, feature engineering, and data-ingestion pipelines.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: ATS compatibility is very strong. The CV uses standard section headings, reverse-chronological experience, conventional text formatting, searchable technology names, and job-relevant terms such as Python, model serving, monitoring, MLflow, Azure, FastAPI, Docker, NLP, transformers, and RAG-related technologies. The likely AI/ATS screening probability is high for the supported requirements, approximately 85–90%. The main keyword opportunity is to make the exact phrase “retrieval-augmented generation (RAG)” more prominent rather than relying mainly on “Retrieval-Augmented Question Answering Demo.” Do not add keywords such as Airflow, Kubeflow, AWS, GCP, Kubernetes, feature engineering, or data versioning because they are not supported by the candidate information.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The CV aligns very well with the role's core work: production NLP systems, document and text classification, transformer fine-tuning, model serving, Azure deployment, production monitoring, dataset preparation, and customer-support-related complaint classification. The RAG project gives the candidate relevant AI-product exposure, although it is clearly a weekend prototype rather than a production system. The degree, Python, Azure, MLflow, model serving, and monitoring requirements are shown. The candidate's material shows gaps in the exact requirement of at least four years specifically as a Machine Learning Engineer shipping systems to production, data versioning, and feature engineering/data-ingestion pipelines. These are job-alignment gaps rather than CV defects. Culture alignment is not directly evidenced in the CV, but mentoring, teaching, production ownership, and incident resolution provide some indirect evidence of collaboration, learning, and ownership.
critique.improvement_instructions:
MINOR, HIGH-VALUE ATS IMPROVEMENT:
1. In the Selected Project title, change “Retrieval-Augmented Question Answering Demo” to “Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) Question-Answering Demo.” Keep the existing description stating that it was a weekend prototype, not used in production, and checked only manually. This adds the job advertisement's exact RAG terminology without overstating the experience.

2. In the Professional Summary, add one concise sentence after the production-monitoring sentence: “Built a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) question-answering prototype over Croatian laws using sentence-transformers, FAISS, and an open-weight LLM accessed through an API.” Retain the project’s existing prototype disclaimer in the Selected Project section; do not describe this as a production product or imply formal evaluation.
